hints.title: Meeting Node Decomposition
hints.text: The optimal subgraph consists of a path from src1 to an intermediate meeting vertex x, a path from src2 to x, and a path from x to dest.

hints.title: Reverse Graph for Destination
hints.text: Running shortest paths backwards from dest on the transposed graph yields the shortest distance from every vertex x to dest.

hints.title: Three Dijkstra Executions
hints.text: Compute d1 from src1, d2 from src2, and d_dest from dest on reversed edges using Dijkstra.

hints.title: Sum of Distances Minimization

complexity.notes: Three Dijkstra runs on graphs with n vertices and m edges.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching paths from src1 and src2 independently without a common meeting vertex fails to share common edges.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency lists and distance vectors use linear O(V + E) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate formulates common meeting node x and runs backward Dijkstra from dest.
